evidence: grep -n 'account_closed_pnl_for_trade' scripts/ops/backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py scripts/ops/backfill_orphan_pnl.py -> both import and call the same function (backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py:79,193; backfill_orphan_pnl.py:...). sed -n '150,242p' scripts/ops/backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py shows _plan_row taking rec.get('closed_pnl') and writing updates={'pnl':..., 'exit_price':...} directly once avg_exit_price>0, with no sign check anywhere in the function. sed -n '200,247p' scripts/ops/backfill_orphan_pnl.py shows the sibling's explicit guard, comment-dated '2026-06-20 dashboard-audit', citing a real incident: 'observed on the bybit_1 DEMO account, where every long resolved to an identical +3847.29 even though the exit was ~18% adverse to entry'. grep -rn backfill_monitor_closed_pnl .github/workflows/system-actions.yml scripts/ops/backfill_monitor_closed_pnl_action.sh confirms this script is dispatchable for real accounts via the system-actions workflow action 'backfill-monitor-closed-pnl' -> backfill_monitor_closed_pnl_action.sh --apply. grep of tests/test_backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py test names found none referencing a sign/mismatch/adverse/favorable case.
expected: A script that writes broker-recovered pnl/exit_price into a real trade's journal row via the same lookup function that already produced one fabricated-profit incident should carry the same defense its sibling already carries.
actual: No sign-consistency guard exists in backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py; a mismatched Bybit closed-pnl record would be written verbatim under --apply.
population: 2 sibling scripts compared (backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py, backfill_orphan_pnl.py) sharing 1 lookup function (account_closed_pnl_for_trade); dispatchable via 1 system-actions workflow verb.
detector: No detector exists today (no test exercises a mismatched-record case for this script). Proposed: port backfill_orphan_pnl.py's guard verbatim or extract it to a shared helper both scripts call, plus a unit test asserting refusal on a sign-inverted fixture.
proposed_fix: Extract the sign-consistency check from backfill_orphan_pnl.py into a shared helper (e.g. src/units/accounts/clients.py or a small scripts/ops helper) and call it from both backfill_orphan_pnl.py and backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py, so the two cannot drift apart again.

Separately: python3 scripts/ops/pipeline.py --help lists only --self-test/--check/--due/--stats/--mint-id/--store -- no verb appends a new record; filing requires calling pipeline.append(item, store, intent=...) from Python directly, which is not documented anywhere as a runnable command.
expected: A binding, frequently-cited operational doc describing a mechanism should match the mechanism's current implementation, and a session should be able to follow the doc's instructions mechanically to file a finding.
actual: Following CLAUDE.md literally (e.g. appending a JSON line to docs/claude/work/PIPELINE.jsonl) would create a file the real reader (read_log(), which defaults to the directory STORE) never consults -- though scripts/ops/pipeline.py's own --check DOES detect and loudly error on exactly this 'resurrected flat file' scenario (see _resurrected_legacy_file()), so the mistake is caught by CI on the next pipeline-guard run, not silently forever.

claim: Several in-scope backfill/journal scripts (backfill_fabricated_exits.py, backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py, backfill_orphan_pnl.py, close_stranded_journal_row.py) truncate a serialized JSON 'notes' blob with a blind string slice (json.dumps(...)[:N]) before writing, which can land mid-escape-sequence and produce invalid JSON; every reader of that column falls back to `{}` on a parse failure, silently discarding the ENTIRE prior notes/audit trail, not just the newest addition.
evidence: grep -n 'json.dumps(new_notes' scripts/ops/backfill_fabricated_exits.py scripts/ops/backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py scripts/ops/backfill_orphan_pnl.py scripts/ops/close_stranded_journal_row.py shows the [:2000]/[:4000] slice pattern in each. backfill_orphan_pnl.py's and backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py's own comments document a real prior incident from exactly this failure mode (issue #1420, cap raised 500->4000 chars after 11 rows lost original_pnl) -- i.e. the fix already applied once widened the threshold rather than removing the class of bug. No live evidence was found that this has recurred since the cap was raised; reported as a design smell / recurring defect class, not a confirmed current corruption.
expected: A truncation strategy that cannot produce invalid JSON (e.g. truncate individual field values before serializing, or drop the oldest audit-trail entries first) rather than a blind post-serialization character slice.
actual: The blind slice pattern still exists in at least 4 in-scope files (and reportedly 3 more out-of-scope siblings), unchanged since the 4000-char cap raise.
population: 4 files in CA-A11's own scope (a wider recurrence exists in CA-A12's scope: rebuild_pnl_from_bybit.py, reconcile_orphan_history.py, revert_backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py -- not claimed as part of this lane's measured population).
detector: None -- no test constructs a notes payload that lands exactly at the truncation boundary with an open escape sequence.
proposed_fix: Replace json.dumps(...)[:N] with a construction that guarantees valid JSON under truncation (e.g. serialize, and if over length, drop oldest keys/entries and re-serialize, rather than slicing the string).
